title: How far off is an angle guess?
description: In a guessing game, one team makes a secret angle and the other team guesses its size. The true size is read with a protractor, and the smaller number is taken from the bigger number to find how far off the guess was. Keeko thinks guessing is pointless when a protractor is there.
teaching_notes: One idea: how far off a guess is equals the bigger number minus the smaller number, whichever of the two is bigger. Watch for students who subtract the true size from the guess even when the guess is smaller.

source: Angle guessing game with two teams. Team 1 secretly chooses
video_script.why: The child learns to compare a guessed angle with its true measure, and to find how far off the guess was by taking the smaller number from the bigger one.
video_script.substitution: The first game of the book: a true angle of forty nine degrees and a guess of thirty nine degrees.
video_script.anchor: an angle drawn on a board, with a protractor beside it and a guess written next to the angle
video_script.wrong_answer: guessing is pointless when a protractor is there to tell us
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko thinks guessing is pointless when a protractor is there to tell us. A protractor is not always at hand, and a guessed size can catch a wrong reading, so the doubt is struck.
video_script.payoff_line: Team two gets ten as its penalty
maths_rules: the gap between the guess and the true measure = the bigger number minus the smaller number = 49 - 39 = 10 degrees
it does not matter whether the guess is too small or too big, the gap is found the same way
in the book the team that guesses gets as many points as the gap, and the lowest total over five turns wins
check: counting up from 39 to 49 takes 10 steps
video_script.design: One idea: the gap between a guess and the true measure is the smaller number taken from the bigger number. The angle stays on the board all video, and the two numbers sit side by side on a number line.
open_questions: The book calls the gap the score in points. The video calls it a penalty, and says that the lowest total wins.
